analysis: The morning belongs to the AI/capex complex: SpaceX's profit beat and merger-committee news (+9.5%), Super Micro's big guidance raise (+11-13%), and Nvidia's Rubin DSX Pods announcement are all concrete AI-demand data points, lifting semis (Micron +3.1%, SOXX +1%) and the Nasdaq while the S&P lags at +0.26% — though the Russell 2000's +0.47% shows the advance has some breadth. Versus the 7am brief, the 'beats aren't enough' theme hardened: AT&T (-6%) and Intuitive Surgical (-6.5%) join Netflix (-7%) as proof that guidance and forward catalysts, not EPS beats, are moving stocks. The crude $100 touch and hot UK CPI are the main risk overhangs into the EIA data and the 20-year auction. Tonight's Meta/Tesla double-header (options implying ±10.6% and ±6.5%) is the week's pivot. Nothing new on USAC; Q3 distribution terms and the Nov 3 earnings date carry forward. No qualifying HN/Reddit threads found this run.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: SpaceX shares +9.5% in morning trading, powering the Nasdaq — swung to a Q3 profit, and Elon Musk said the boards of SpaceX and Tesla formed committees to discuss a merger.
headlines.why_it_matters: Blowout quarter plus genuine merger-exploration news — the session's main upside driver and sentiment tailwind for the AI complex.

headlines.headline: Tesla +2.5% ahead of Q3 results after the close (5:30 PM ET). Street expects EPS ~$0.44-0.45 (down ~10% YoY) and revenue ~$27.8-27.9B (-0.5% YoY); Q3 deliveries of 486,532 already beat the 463,761 estimate, so margins and cash flow are the focus.
headlines.why_it_matters: Deliveries already known — the move will come from auto margins (consensus ~18%), robotaxi/FSD updates, and the SpaceX merger committee read-through.

headlines.headline: Meta roughly flat to slightly lower (-0.3%) ahead of Q3 results after the close (4:30 PM ET). Consensus: revenue $63.18B, EPS $6.67; options imply a ±10.57% move. Wall Street is watching whether ad growth covers AI capex and whether the Muse AI agent is inflecting revenue.
headlines.why_it_matters: Largest implied earnings move of the day — tonight's print sets the tape for the AI-capex debate into Thursday.

headlines.headline: Nvidia +1.9% as CEO Jensen Huang announced Vera Rubin DSX Pods — data centers designed to be deployed in days rather than months. FactSet now has Micron and Nvidia as the top two contributors to S&P 500 Q3 earnings growth.
headlines.why_it_matters: Product catalyst plus top earnings-growth contributor status — supports the morning's AI-stock rotation after yesterday's slip.

headlines.headline: Super Micro +11-13% after raising Q1 revenue guidance to $18.5-19.5B from $14.5-15.5B, citing AI demand. Micron +3.1%, Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) +2%, semis (SOXX) +1%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Big guidance raise is a concrete AI-capex data point — the read-through lifting the whole memory/semiconductor complex this morning.

headlines.headline: Netflix -7% after beating Q3 earnings but issuing soft Q4 revenue guidance — failed to ease concerns about slowing engagement.
headlines.why_it_matters: Beats aren't enough this quarter — guidance is what moves the stock, a bearish signal for other growth names reporting this week.

headlines.headline: AT&T -6% despite better-than-expected Q3 results, with revenue up 5.3% to $32.3B. Also lower: Intuitive Surgical -6.5% (beat Q3 but disclosed a $450M antitrust settlement and narrowed its procedure-growth outlook).
headlines.why_it_matters: More evidence of the harsh post-earnings bar — investors are selling the news on beats lacking a forward catalyst.

headlines.headline: Crude spiked intraday — US crude briefly touched $100 a barrel and Brent traded near $111, while UK inflation printed hot at 3.5%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Energy-price spike plus hot UK CPI are upside inflation risks — watch whether they pull yields higher into the 20-year auction.
